canonical_name: SimpleKalmanFilter -- a compact scalar Kalman filter (Denys Sene)
lineage: Kalman filter (1960, Rudolf Kalman): recursive least-squares estimation of hidden state from noisy measurements via predict/update; this is a minimal scalar C++ reference for embedded sensor smoothing
version: github.com/denyssene/SimpleKalmanFilter master as of 2026-09-12 (commit in hashes)
build_system: compile the .cpp with a Techne driver

example.command: Techne harness: a constant true value + Gaussian measurement noise; check the filtered variance << raw variance
example.input: noisy measurements of a hidden constant
example.output: an estimate whose error variance is far below the measurement noise

upstream_docs: Kalman, A New Approach to Linear Filtering and Prediction Problems, 1960

human_capability_summary.built_to: recover a hidden true value from a stream of noisy measurements by recursively combining a prediction with each new observation, weighted by their uncertainties
human_capability_summary.pressure: measurement noise and the impossibility of observing the true state directly; a naive average lags, a raw reading is jittery
human_capability_summary.success_means: an estimate that tracks the true state with error variance far below the raw measurement noise

known_human_problem_solved: optimal recursive estimation of hidden state under noise
human_failure_condition: a mistuned filter either lags reality (over-smooths) or passes the noise through (under-smooths); a navigation estimate drifts and the vehicle mislocates
behavioral_entry_point: raise the measurement-noise level, or feed a step change in the hidden value, and watch the estimate's lag/variance trade-off

nyx_handoff.how_to_run_it: recipe.json (runner docker); python -m techne.fossils.harvest run simple-kalman-denyssene
nyx_handoff.what_humans_used_it_for: recover a hidden true value from a stream of noisy measurements by recursively combining a prediction with each new observation, weighted by their uncertainties
